We just published a list of the 10 Stocks Analysts Upgraded On Monday and Airbnb (NASDAQ:ABNB) ranked 9th on this list.

A broad selloff dragged US stocks lower on November 16, as Reuters reported that the exit of the founder of the world's most closely watched AI chipmaker as chief executive had soured enthusiasm for AI shares. The chipmaker's shares had just logged their longest weekly losing streak since October 2012, and a Reuters columnist wrote that investors have been warned about a possible market top, though timing one is nearly impossible.

The damage was heaviest in technology. Reuters reported that chipmakers fell between 3.5% and 5% in premarket trading on November 16, while server makers dropped as much as 5.1%. Since October 6, the S&P 500 technology sector has fallen 20% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor index has fallen 30%.

10 Best US Stocks to Buy Under $25
AI Selloff Leaves Beaten-Down Stocks in Focus

A selloff this deep tends to send investors looking for names that fell too far. Swissquote senior analyst Ipek Ozkardeskaya warned that buyers of a hotly awaited AI developer's market debut later in the week may sell existing tech holdings to pay for it, so a strong debut might not lift every AI stock.

Readers sorting through the wreckage can look at which beaten-down AI stocks analysts still see rising 50% or morein one of our rankings.

Rate Hike Bets Add to the Pressure

Interest rates are pulling in the same direction. Reuters reported that markets fully price a rate hike in December after hotter-than-expected inflation data, and CME FedWatch put the chance of a 50-basis-point increase at about 8%. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the economy will likely need "several interest rate increases" before spring 2027 to restore price stability. Rate futures price in only about three 25-basis-point hikes by mid-2027.

Safe havens have not helped. Treasury yields are under pressure from rate-hike expectations and sticky inflation, gold fell below $4,000 to a one-year low, and the US dollar has been the main winner. Fed officials made 19 public appearances in one week after 20 the week before.

Some stocks have held up better than the rest. Our list of stocks trading near all-time highs that Wall Street still likesshows where analysts still see room to run.

Bank of America Global Research economists expect the minutes of the October Fed meeting to show a deeper split over holding rates than the 10-2 vote suggested. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh was due to speak in San Francisco on November 16, and 2-year Treasury yields had just posted their largest weekly rise in over two years.

Airbnb made it to our list because it has an average upside potential of 11%. PhillipCapital upgraded Airbnb from Reduce to Neutral on November 16 and raised its price target to $184 from $158, citing a sharp pickup in bookings. PhillipCapital stopped short of a Buy rating.

Airbnb runs an online marketplace that connects hosts with travelers looking for a place to stay. In the third quarter of 2026, reported on November 5, revenue rose 19% to $4.87 billion. Nights and seats booked grew 16% to 155.0 million, slower than the 19% rise in revenue. The board also authorized a $12 billion share buyback, the company raised its full-year revenue growth outlook to the high teens, and it guided fourth-quarter revenue to between $3.22 billion and $3.28 billion.

Bulls call the third quarter a blowout, and much of the commentary since has asked whether the stock still has room to run after its jump on the results. PhillipCapital's own move shows how that debate splits, since the firm went from Reduce to Neutral and not further. Whether growth like this justifies a premium valuation is the subject of our piece on Airbnb's growth against its peers' multiples.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of ABNB as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. Today's big story: Anthropic IPO: Priced For 2031, Or 2036?

Booking Holdings (BKNG) expects its room nights to grow 1% to 3% in the fourth quarter of 2026. Management gave that guidance on its November 3, 2026 call. Room nights are the nights travelers book through its sites. They offer the plainest count of the travel Booking sells. The guidance would mark a clear slowdown from the third quarter. So why is Booking expecting room-night growth to slow?

Why Booking Holdings Expects Slower Room-Night Growth

Management gave two reasons for the slower growth. Booking faces its toughest year-earlier comparison of 2026. It is also unsure how recent events will affect travel demand. In October, demand was hit by disrupted travel to and from the Middle East, elevated airfares and localized unrest in certain European cities. Management's guide assumes the effects of the Middle East conflict last through the end of the year.

Room nights grew 7% in the third quarter, accelerating from 5% in the second quarter and topping management's own guidance.

Booking also expects slower sales growth and flat profit. Management expects adjusted revenue, the company's own measure, to grow 0% to 2% in the fourth quarter, after rising 9% in the third. It expects adjusted EBITDA, a profit measure, to be about flat from a year earlier. Part of the reason is that it plans to spend more on flights, attractions, dining and AI.

Will Booking Holdings' Slowdown Last Into 2027?

Management has not said yet. The company plans to discuss 2027 in February with its fourth-quarter results. Executives did offer early signs on both sides.

On the hopeful side, management said its on-the-book statistics for the first half of 2027 look healthy. It called them a very early indicator, still subject to cancellations. Booking's alternative accommodation listings grew 9% in the third quarter. Management called that an encouraging signal for future growth in that category.

On the other side, management said travel demand was resilient in the third quarter but moderated somewhat toward its end. How long the slowdown lasts remains an open question for holders.

How Hard Has Booking Holdings Stock Been Hit?

Booking Holdings stock has lost 22.8% over the past year, against a 10.3% gain for the S&P 500. The shares trade at 16.1 times earnings, against 22.0 for the S&P 500. At the end of September, before the outlook, Booking's P/E was already the second lowest of 40 quarter ends since December 2016. Today's 16.1 is lower still, so the price likely assumes slower growth ahead.

title: Airbnb vs. Shopify: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
detail:
Airbnb vs. Shopify: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
Jake Lerch, The Motley Fool
Wed, November 18, 2026 at 7:05 AM MST 6 min read
ABNB
SHOP
AMZN
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Will the future of growth be driven by global travel experiences or the expansion of independent digital commerce? Deciding between Airbnb (NASDAQ:ABNB)and Shopify (NASDAQ:SHOP)involves choosing between two very different platform leaders.

Airbnb connects millions of travelers with unique stays, while Shopify provides the software backbone for modern retail. Both companies benefit from powerful network effects, where more users or merchants make the platform more valuable for everyone involved.

The case for Airbnb

Airbnb operates as a massive marketplace for lodging and experiences, connecting more than 5 million hosts with guests in roughly 220 countries. In its latest annual report, the company highlights its reliance on Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) for platform hosting and its use of third-party providers for community support. As the platform evolves, it is exploring the use of AI in travel to enhance its search capabilities and host support.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $13.9 billion. This represents a revenue growth of approximately 16.7% compared to the prior twelve-month period. During the same time frame, the company reported net income of nearly $3.2 billion.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio, which measures a company's ability to cover its short-term debts with liquid assets, reached roughly 1.4x. The debt-to-equity ratio, which measures total debt relative to shareholders' equity, is approximately 0.3x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was close to $4.6 billion, though note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 34.3% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation.

The case for Shopify

Shopify serves as the central operating system for millions of merchants across 175 countries, providing tools for both online and in-store sales. The company supports everyone from small entrepreneurs to large enterprise brands, relying on partners like PayPal and Stripe for payment processing. This ecosystem approach allows it to scale without owning inventory, creating a software-centric business model with high recurring potential.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached close to $14.2 billion. This reflects a revenue growth of roughly 32.5% over the preceding period. Shopify also reported a net income of approximately $2.1 billion for these twelve months.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio is approximately 6.0x, indicating a strong ability to meet short-term obligations. The debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.0x, indicating a very low level of debt relative to equity. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was nearly $2.0 billion, and stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 22.1% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation.

Risk profile comparison

Airbnb faces significant regulatory hurdles, such as the restrictions on short-term rentals in New York City, which could be adopted by other global cities. The company also competes intensely with major travel platforms like Booking Holdings (NASDAQ:BKNG), Expedia Group (NASDAQ:EXPE), and Trip.com Group (NASDAQ:TCOM), as well as search engines like Alphabet. Furthermore, an ongoing IRS tax audit involving a $1.3 billion claim adds a layer of financial uncertainty to the company's long-term outlook.

Shopify encounters fierce competition from established e-commerce software vendors and massive marketplaces like Amazon. The business is also exposed to cybersecurity risks and data privacy concerns, which have previously led to class action litigation over its collection of buyer information. Since Shopify relies heavily on third-party payment service providers, any disruption in those relationships could impact its ability to process transactions for its merchants.

Valuation comparison

Airbnb appears to be the more conservatively valued stock, carrying both a lower Forward P/E and a lower P/S ratio compared to Shopify. The Forward P/E compares the stock price to future earnings estimates, while the P/S ratio is the market cap divided by sales over the past twelve months.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

When comparing Airbnb and Shopify, investors should consider a few key factors. Let's have a look at them and see what that tells us about each stock.

Firstly, we should consider revenue growth. Here, Shopify can claim an advantage. Over the last three years, the company has averaged year-over-year revenue growth of 28.7%. What's more, in recent quarters, that growth has accelerated, with Shopify delivering 31.6% revenue growth in its most recent quarter. Airbnb's three-year average is 13.5%; its growth has also accelerated, with the company reporting 17.7% revenue growth in its most recent quarter.

Another factor to consider is each company's profitability. Both companies have been consistently profitable in recent years. However, Airbnb can claim an edge in the category. Its operating margin is 22.6%, while Shopify's is 18.1%.

Finally, there's valuation. Since both companies are delivering consistent profits, let's use price-to-earnings (P/E) to compare their valuations. Airbnb stock trades at a P/E multiple of 34x, while Shopify trades at around 87x. That makes Airbnb stock significantly more affordable.

To sum up, investors may want to consider both of these consumer stocks, given their impressive growth rates and profits. However, in this particular head-to-head comparison, Airbnb has the overall edge, in my view. The company's profitability, combined with its more reasonable valuation, complements its revenue growth, which exceeds 15%, making it my choice in this battle of consumer stocks.

Investors who held the shares through that run may wonder whether the easy money is gone, while those on the sidelines might ask if they are too late. So if you bought Airbnb today and held it for three years, what could the shares return, and what would have to go right?

What Would Three Years Of Holding Airbnb Return?

Airbnb's Growth Is Picking Up Again

title: Cathie Wood and Jim Cramer Agree on These 10 Stocks: Latest 13F
detail:
Cathie Wood and Jim Cramer Agree on These 10 Stocks: Latest 13F
Fahad Saleem
Tue, November 17, 2026 at 6:28 AM MST 8 min read
ARKK
^GSPC
SPY
BWXT

Jim Cramer and Cathie Wood are two of the most closely followed voices on Wall Street, and we regularly cover the stocks they like. Once a Wall Street darling, Cathie Wood has struggled to replicate her success from the pandemic days as shifting market dynamics have weighed on her disruptive innovation bets. You can see her latest 13F filing here.

Wood's flagship ARK Innovation ETF (BATS:ARKK) is down about 4% so far this year, while the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up about 10%. ARKK had gained about 16% through the end of September, and a sharp tech selloff in October and early November erased that gain and pushed the fund below where it started the year.  As of Nov. 12, her Ark Innovation ETF has delivered a five-year annualized return of -8.23%, while the S&P 500 has an annualized return of 10.15% over the same period, according to data from Morningstar.

In August, ARK kept buying Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) across five funds while investors worried about an AI bubble, and it sold some Roblox shares. Check out the full story here.

Wood addressed the selloff in her latest In The Know episode on YouTube, and she thinks the market overreacted to the midterm elections. She said stocks have usually risen in the year after a midterm election, by roughly 13% to 14% in the periods she showed. She also tried to calm fears that data center projects will slow down. Wood said data centers in communities like those in Virginia have lowered property taxes and paid for new schools, and she blamed the negative headlines for hiding that. She also thinks AI spending is still at an early stage.

Wood expects AI to lift productivity, keep inflation lower than most investors expect, and push US real GDP growth to 7%. Cramer has also talked about the data center backlash. He said AI executives now face criticism over rising electricity bills, resource use and job losses, and he still likes certain AI stocks. Click to see the stocks he still likes.

Methodology

To compile this list, we reviewed ARK Investment Management's third-quarter 2026 portfolio, as disclosed in its latest 13F filing, and identified stocks that Jim Cramer has spoken positively about in his recent CNBC commentary. We prioritized well-known companies and excluded stocks in which ARK reduced its shareholdings by more than 5% during the quarter. We then ranked the 10 selected stocks in ascending order of the number of hedge funds holding stakes in them at the end of the second quarter of 2026, using Insider Monkey's database of 1,006 hedge funds. ARK's holdings and changes reflect the third quarter, while the hedge fund ownership figures reflect the second quarter. To see where ARK stood going into the year, check our list Cathie Wood 2026 Portfolio: 10 Best Stocks to Buy. For more of Cramer's recent favorites, see Jim Cramer Is Bullish on These 10 Stocks Amid Nvidia (NVDA) Controversy.

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 612% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 375 percentage points (see more details here).

#10. BWX Technologies, Inc. (NYSE:BWXT)

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 65

BWX Technologies, Inc. (NYSE:BWXT) is a nuclear technology company that manufactures nuclear components and systems for the U.S. Navy, government agencies, and commercial nuclear power operators. The company plays a critical role in supplying nuclear propulsion technology for U.S. submarines and aircraft carriers while expanding its presence in the commercial nuclear energy market.

Cathie Wood's ARK Investment Management increased its stake in BWX Technologies by 38% during the third quarter of 2026, ending September with 754,114 shares worth approximately $103.31 million.

Jim Cramer has also expressed a bullish view on BWX Technologies. During a September episode of Mad Money, Cramer said he preferred BWX Technologies over uranium producer Cameco, while emphasizing the long-term opportunities associated with the expansion of nuclear power.

Cramer revisited BWX Technologies later in September, following a 27% decline in its shares over the preceding three months. He highlighted the company's strong underlying operations and praised its investor presentation, during which management outlined ambitious financial targets for 2030. BWX Technologies is targeting annual revenue of $5.5 billion to $6 billion by the end of the decade, supported by growing demand for nuclear technologies in defense and commercial applications.

#9. Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB)

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 75

Cathie Wood's ARK Investment Management increased its Airbnb stake by 48% during the third quarter of 2026, ending September with 218,989 shares worth approximately $35.18 million.

Jim Cramer made a particularly bullish call on Airbnb in September and said investors were overestimating the threat artificial intelligence poses to the company's business.

Cramer said Airbnb was relatively insulated from AI-powered booking agents because finding and booking individual rental properties is more complicated than booking standardized hotel rooms. Following a significant selloff in the stock, he called Airbnb "a steal." Another fund manager has made a similar argument that AI poses limited risk to Airbnb's business. Check the full letter here.

Cramer had previously recommended staying invested in Airbnb during an August episode of Mad Money.

#8. Cloudflare, Inc. (NYSE:NET)

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 87

Cloudflare, Inc. (NYSE:NET) provides cloud-based networking, security, and application services that help businesses improve website performance, protect their digital infrastructure, and manage internet traffic. The company is increasingly positioning itself as an important infrastructure provider for the growing use of AI agents.

ARK Investment Management aggressively increased its Cloudflare holdings in the third quarter, boosting its position by 221%. The fund held 563,167 shares worth approximately $195.58 million at the end of September. Growth fund managers have also pointed to Cloudflare as a winner from the rise of AI agents. Click to read the full letter.

Jim Cramer expressed strong enthusiasm for Cloudflare's business during an October episode of Mad Money. He highlighted the company's role in managing the enormous volume of internet traffic generated by AI agents.

He also pointed to Cloudflare's accelerating revenue growth and its position in the content delivery network market.

Cramer distinguished his enthusiasm for the company from his willingness to purchase shares at elevated valuations. Although he said he loved Cloudflare, he recommended waiting for a meaningful marketwide pullback before buying the stock. Cloudflare's own finance chief has said the company's opportunity could be much larger than its current business. See what management said here.

#7. DoorDash, Inc. (NASDAQ:DASH)

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 107

Cathie Wood's ARK Investment Management increased its DoorDash position by 3% in the third quarter, ending September with 388,357 shares valued at approximately $71.28 million.

Jim Cramer explicitly recommended buying DoorDash during a May episode of Mad Money, despite the company's shares having suffered a substantial decline.

Cramer argued that investors were abandoning businesses such as DoorDash and Uber in favor of semiconductor stocks, creating opportunities in companies whose underlying businesses remained attractive.

He also defended DoorDash against concerns that AI agents could disrupt online marketplaces. In September, Cramer questioned the assumption that artificial intelligence would eliminate the competitive advantages enjoyed by established delivery platforms. DoorDash keeps growing its sales, but its shares have trailed the market this year. Click to see if the dip is worth buying.

#6. Tesla, Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA)

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 116

Tesla, Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA) is an electric vehicle and energy company whose investment story increasingly revolves around autonomous driving, robotics, and Elon Musk's broader technology ambitions.

Tesla remained Cathie Wood's largest disclosed holding at the end of the third quarter of 2026. ARK Investment Management increased its stake by 23%, ending September with 3.37 million shares worth approximately $1.20 billion. The stock accounted for 6.89% of its reported portfolio. Wood has built much of her Tesla case around robotaxis and humanoid robots. Click to see if she was right.

Jim Cramer's bullish view on Tesla has recently been closely tied to SpaceX rather than the electric vehicle business alone.

During his October CNBC commentary, Cramer explicitly recommended buying Tesla for investors who believed in SpaceX. He suggested that developments involving Musk's space and AI infrastructure business could provide an important catalyst for Tesla.

Cramer reaffirmed that view during another October episode of Mad Money. Asked whether Tesla was a buy, sell, or hold, he said his strong belief in SpaceX also made him a believer in Tesla, although he preferred SpaceX itself.

Today's big story: Could Nvidia Stock Fall 50%? Follow The Cash

Expedia (EXPE) stock fell 4.8% over the past year, while the S&P 500 returned 11.4%. The company continued to repurchase its own shares anyway. In the four quarters to September 2026, Expedia spent an amount equal to 5.3% of its current market value on buybacks, net of stock paid to employees. So how much more does each Expedia share earn because of the buybacks?

How Much More Each Expedia Share Now Earns

Over the past three years, Expedia's earnings per share grew 45.4% a year, against 35.8% a year for its net income. That is a gap of 9.7 percentage points a year. Each share earned more than profit growth alone would give it because there were fewer shares to split that profit among: the diluted share count fell from 148 million in the twelve months to September 2023 to 122 million in the twelve months to September 2026.

The number of shares you hold remains the same. Each one simply claims a larger slice of Expedia's earnings, though the market value of that slice still depends on the share price.

Expedia Pays For Its Buybacks Out Of Cash Flow

Expedia covers the buybacks with cash generated by its travel business, which continues to expand. Revenue in the business-to-business (B2B) segment grew 18.0% in fiscal 2025, compared with 2.2% for the business-to-customer side, which is still the larger of the two.

In the twelve months to September 30, 2026, Expedia generated free cash flow equal to 1.6 times the $2.28 billion it distributed through buybacks and dividends. During a November 4, 2026 call, management said this cash has fueled the return of capital to shareholders.

Expedia also reduced its debt burden while repurchasing shares. Total debt fell to $5.69 billion at September 30, 2026, down from $6.48 billion a year earlier. Cash and short-term investments of $5.57 billion nearly match that debt. Over the past twelve months, operating income covered interest expense 8.4 times.

Why Expedia's Expected Slowdown Matters To Shareholders

Profit growth, rather than a smaller share count, drove most of the earnings increase for each Expedia share. Because of this, a business slowdown would show up in what each share earns.

Management expects the business to slow in fiscal Q4 2026, guiding for revenue growth of 4% to 5.7%, compared with the 11.9% reported for fiscal Q3 2026. Management pointed to the timing of its fall sale, which pulled demand into the third quarter, and cited a softer environment that includes the U.S. election cycle and travel disruptions across EMEA. The company still raised its full-year forecast after the third quarter came in above the high end of its own guidance.
